mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and drives lower S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% over three months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% and CPIAUCSL falls > -0.5% over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.6%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth > 0.4% monthly for two months) and a rise in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals strengthening residential demand, which boosts construction and related equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.4% for 2 months AND HOUST > 5% for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals a tight labor market, which raises wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for 4 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% over same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (implied by RSAFS growth > 1% monthly for three consecutive months) while consumption growth (GDPC1) is flat signals a precautionary savings regime, which reduces near-term consumption demand and corporate revenues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 1% for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 change < 0.1% over same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (< -0.3%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
